rules: Append-only: an entry is never renamed or removed. A new meaning gets a new entry; a retired wire kind keeps its entry with status retired.
`wire` is the kind on the v2 protocol (crates/rth-protocol); `name` is the plain past-tense fact a person reads.
Old history is never rewritten: readers map wire kinds through this file.
`summary` is a template over the event's own fields; `{field}` is replaced, `values` maps raw field values to plain words.

phases.input: something arrived from a person or a sense
phases.decision: the agent chose what to do
phases.agent: the agent's own state and health

events.name: message_audio_added
events.note: generated agent audio, not heard audio; added after the v3 table

events.name: input_audio_added
events.note: captured input audio, silence and noise included; not evidence of speech or speaker

events.name: input_audio_ended
events.note: a transport stream ended or paused, not necessarily an utterance; the ingress receipt says what arrived

events.name: input_audio_received
events.note: the guest receipt for a stream (counts and hash), not evidence the model heard it

events.name: speech_transcribed
events.note: provider transcription, possibly incremental; implies neither finality nor speaker identity

events.name: provider_turn_signaled
events.note: observed provider state, separate from local completion

events.name: message_playback_reported
events.note: one kind for started, finished and cleared; played_samples are samples handed to the device or sink, never proof of being heard
events.summary: {response_id} playback {phase}: {played_samples} samples handed to device, {dropped_samples} dropped

events.name: command_submitted
events.note: a typed command for the rolling session, sent by the host control owner; a submission, not yet an admission, and a retry resends the identical frame

events.name: command_admitted
events.note: sent only after the command record is fsynced to the durable command log; admission proves neither that the effect ran nor that the reply finished. A retry (duplicate) reports the recorded state, which can be interrupted

status.interrupted: interrupted (agent restarted before a result was recorded)

events.name: media_stored
events.note: a durable, content-addressed copy of PCM (rth.media-ref/v1): written only after the blob and its directory entry were fsynced. Generated agent audio or captured microphone audio, never evidence of being played or heard. Chunks with no covering media_stored were never made durable

events.name: model_context_checked
events.note: what a boot did with the model's conversation context: restored = the backend state the previous process held, partial = a text-history approximation given to the provider, not_restored = empty context. History bytes are retained in every case and no effect is replayed

events.name: response_outcome_detailed
events.note: the detail behind a reply's one terminal; never a terminal itself: message_finished stays the only one, and this follows it. cause is the reply's decision; terminal_event_id is the exact message_finished it details. provider_status is the provider's own open-ended string (incomplete maps to failed); provider_reason is null when the provider gave none and is never made up. outcome_source local means the provider gave no outcome (local_reason: cancel_unacknowledged, unassociated, create_rejected, session_ended, no_session); local_reason after_local_terminal marks a provider outcome that arrived after a local terminal, metadata only

events.name: task_ledger_ready
events.note: the agent's task ledger is open and recovered; sent once per connection, only by an agent built with delegation on. A separate kind, not a Hello field, so no Hello literal changes

events.name: task_state_recorded
events.note: one committed ledger transition or refused update; record is the full task snapshot; cause is the task_update or executor_status it answers (the host owner's receipt)

events.name: task_progress_reported
events.note: an executor report forwarded by the host owner (POST /v1/tasks/<id>)
events.summary: the report worker reported progress on task {task_id}

events.name: task_worker_status_reported
events.note: the executor lease, or a launcher exit receipt the host owner authenticated (the proof never crosses the link)
events.summary: the report worker's status was reported

events.name: memory_act_recorded
events.note: one memory act (remember or correct) fsynced in the agent's memory ledger before its tool output went to the model. state committed changes the items; proposed (no trusted acceptance: not a typed request) and rejected (with a reason) change nothing. A correction appends a revision; nothing is rewritten. Provenance (provider call, typed command) is filled by the agent, never by the model

events.name: memory_recalled
events.note: a recall receipt. count and total are the saved items this recall selected locally from the memory ledger (ids and revisions, never their text); recall.status says what became of them: held, enqueued (queued for the backend), backend_closed or dropped_context_changed (not delivered), selected_by_backend (the backend selected the text; that receipt repeats no items), dropped_context_changed_at_backend. A receipt is not evidence that the model received or used anything
events.summary: recall receipt {call_id}: {count} of {total} saved items selected locally

field_notes.note: text is a delta; the utterance text is its parts concatenated in utterance_seq order. utterance_id is minted locally by the agent's backend adapter, never a provider id; boundaries come only from the provider's end-of-transcription flag (final), never from model turns; boundary=local marks an utterance that began at a local split. final is true only when the provider's flag was parsed. response_id with association=provider only with real identity evidence (the fake backend); Gemini parts are always association=unknown (arrival order is not evidence)
for a provider-opened response, the locally minted utterance it answers, only with identity evidence (absent for Gemini)
for a provider-opened decision, the locally minted utterance it answers, only with identity evidence (absent for Gemini)

instance.context is one of restored | partial | not_restored (or the legacy history_retained_model_context_not_restored); instance.context_restore carries status, method, snapshot, watermark, lineage_since, turns, tail_records, truncated_turns, detail
the journaled copy has data "" from the media-sidecar build on; its PCM is in the media_stored blob covering its chunk. Records with non-empty data (older builds) are read inline

field_notes.source: provider turn boundaries and OpenAI Realtime
field_notes.note: supersedes the note above on two points. Boundaries: a final part still ends its utterance, but Gemini (which does not send its end-of-transcription flag in practice) also ends one at a provider turn boundary: its own voice-activity start, or, in a session with no voice activity, a model turn's end; the next utterance's first part has boundary=provider_turn. A boundary is never a link to a reply. Association: OpenAI Realtime parts have one utterance per provider input item, and carry association=provider_adjacent with the reply's response_id once the provider placed that reply's output item right after this item; that is adjacency in the conversation, not proof the reply answers it. Anything else stays association=unknown

supersedes the two notes above where they differ. OpenAI Realtime parts carry no response_id and are always association=unknown: a conversation position (previous_item_id) is not an answers-to link, so association=provider_adjacent is not emitted, and no decision or message_started names an utterance for OpenAI. boundary=provider_turn is display segmentation only: the segment after it may begin mid-utterance and is never restored as settled input, even when the provider finishes it. boundary=local also follows a completion the agent rejected because it did not extend the parts already shown; those parts are never final
